title: One Forest, Different Ways to Live

scenes.tts: Several kinds of warblers hunt insects in the same spruce forest. How can they share one place without running out of food? Watch the same tree as the birds choose where to search. Gold outlines the shared forest, while each bird keeps its own color.
scenes.narration: Several kinds of warblers hunt insects in the same spruce forest. How can they share one place without running out of food? Watch the same tree as the birds choose where to search. Gold outlines the shared forest, while each bird keeps its own color.
scenes.visual: Hook first. A large schematic spruce fills at least sixty percent of the frame. Show the label 'FIVE KINDS' on screen, not in speech. Five simple bird silhouettes enter together and chase moving insect dots. Color map for both films: habitat outline GOLD; insects YELLOW; Cape May TEAL; Blackburnian ORANGE; black-throated green GREEN; bay-breasted PURPLE; myrtle RED. Birds cross paths while insects drift among branches. Mark all biological motion 'schematic'.
Keep the spruce visible and moving gently. Bring in the title 'One Forest, Different Ways to Live' for two seconds, then transform its underline into the gold habitat outline.

scenes.tts: The spruce forest is their habitat, the place where they live. A niche is different. It is an organism's role: how it lives and uses resources there. Food is part of a niche. So are where and when it feeds, the space it uses, what eats it, and its ecosystem role.
scenes.narration: The spruce forest is their habitat, the place where they live. A niche is different. It is an organism's role: how it lives and uses resources there. Food is part of a niche. So are where and when it feeds, the space it uses, what eats it, and its ecosystem role.
scenes.visual: The gold outline closes around the whole spruce and becomes the label 'HABITAT: PLACE'. Then colored paths grow behind the moving birds. One path circles outer tips, another crosses inner branches, and others favor different heights. Transform 'PLACE' into 'NICHE: WAY OF LIVING' beside the paths. Small icon labels appear only as named and orbit the tree: food, place and time, space, predators, ecosystem role.

scenes.tts: A resource is something a living thing needs and takes from its habitat. Food, water, shelter, and space are resources. Each warbler searches spruce needles with its small, thin bill. Finding insects supplies food, and food helps the bird survive.
scenes.narration: A resource is something a living thing needs and takes from its habitat. Food, water, shelter, and space are resources. Each warbler searches spruce needles with its small, thin bill. Finding insects supplies food, and food helps the bird survive.
scenes.visual: Keep the tree and color paths. Yellow insect dots settle among enlarged needle clusters before the label 'FOOD RESOURCE' appears. Each colored bird follows its path and removes one dot. A small energy bar beside each bird rises. Water, shelter, and space icons briefly grow from the same tree, then fold back into the tree.

scenes.tts: When organisms need the same resource and it is in short supply, they compete. Competition is a struggle for resources in short supply. If birds search the same branches, they may reach for the same insect. Their niches overlap where their resource use overlaps.
scenes.narration: When organisms need the same resource and it is in short supply, they compete. Competition is a struggle for resources in short supply. If birds search the same branches, they may reach for the same insect. Their niches overlap where their resource use overlaps.
scenes.visual: Insect dots slowly become fewer. Two colored paths now cross on one branch. Both birds approach the same remaining insect, but only one reaches it. A red pulse marks the shared reach, then expands into a translucent region labelled 'OVERLAP'. Keep the other birds moving softly elsewhere.

scenes.tts: A species is one kind of living thing. The warblers are different species, even though their bodies and food look similar. Competition can leave one kind with enough food and another short. It becomes more likely when their shared resource is scarce.
scenes.narration: A species is one kind of living thing. The warblers are different species, even though their bodies and food look similar. Competition can leave one kind with enough food and another short. It becomes more likely when their shared resource is scarce.
scenes.visual: Keep the on-screen label 'MODEL — SCHEMATIC'. The five birds line up briefly beside their fixed colors while the shared spruce stays large behind them. Transform the line back into moving birds. One bird reaches a yellow insect and its food bar fills; another arrives later and its bar remains short. Keep the red overlap region pulsing gently.

scenes.tts: Now predict. Insects become scarce, and every kind searches every branch. Will more birds get enough food, or will more fall short? Keep your answer while the insect dots fade.
scenes.narration: Now predict. Insects become scarce, and every kind searches every branch. Will more birds get enough food, or will more fall short? Keep your answer while the insect dots fade.
scenes.visual: All five colored paths spread across the whole tree as yellow dots fade to a few. Show the question in large text. Beneath the tree, two unlabeled outcome bars wait without revealing an answer. Mark the setup 'schematic'.
Hold the question and nearly empty tree. Birds continue slow searching motion. A thin thinking ring fills once during the pause; do not reveal the answer.

scenes.tts: With scarce insects and every kind searching everywhere, more kinds are likely to fall short in this simple model. Now let each color favor its own tree zone. The birds still share one forest, but fewer paths cross. Different niches can reduce competition when insects are limited. That can help more kinds share the habitat.
scenes.narration: With scarce insects and every kind searching everywhere, more kinds are likely to fall short in this simple model. Now let each color favor its own tree zone. The birds still share one forest, but fewer paths cross. Different niches can reduce competition when insects are limited. That can help more kinds share the habitat.
scenes.visual: Fill the 'fall short' outcome bar, labelled 'MODEL RESULT'. Then transform the full-tree paths into preferred zones without cutting away. Each color remains visible and some edges overlap. Refill a few insect dots at the same rate in every zone. Red overlap pulses shrink but do not disappear.

scenes.tts: The model simplifies nature. Real niches include much more than feeding zones. Birds also change where they search when food or weather changes. Different use does not remove all competition. It changes the chances of meeting over a limited resource.
scenes.narration: The model simplifies nature. Real niches include much more than feeding zones. Birds also change where they search when food or weather changes. Different use does not remove all competition. It changes the chances of meeting over a limited resource.
scenes.visual: Zoom out slightly. Add a small 'MODEL' frame around the zoned tree. The frame expands into a broader 'REAL NICHE' outline containing food, time, space, predators, and weather icons. A wind arrow bends branches and one bird shifts lower. Keep a small overlap region glowing.

scenes.tts: That gives a testable explanation for the opening puzzle. Shared habitat does not mean identical niche. The next step is evidence: watch where real warblers spent time, then ask what those observations can support.
scenes.narration: That gives a testable explanation for the opening puzzle. Shared habitat does not mean identical niche. The next step is evidence: watch where real warblers spent time, then ask what those observations can support.
scenes.visual: The colored preferred paths settle on the spruce. A stopwatch and pale zone grid slide toward the tree without covering it. Transform 'MODEL' into 'TEST WITH OBSERVATIONS'. Fade narration labels before the end card.
One line only, centered in large type: 'Different niches can reduce competition, helping species share a habitat.' No title, subtitle, logo, or smaller line.
